surfaces.part: scrap parts, folded cloth and rusty can on the counter

answer.evidence: The roof fills rows 1-13 as a sloped burlap plane with patches (a green patch at rows 4-8). Row 13 is a light front-edge line, followed by dark eave shadow at rows 14-15. Below it the stall front is drawn from rows 16-31: a dark interior with goods on the counter (rows 17-22) over a crate front with planks and braces (rows 23-31). The width stays at 46-48 px with no receding side face. The roof is 13 rows tall, so it is a real top surface and not a rim.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a burlap-roofed stall with a crate counter, and it is the right kind of prop to sit beside prop-stall-cheese. Measured facts: 10 visible tones per tile (hedge 9, stall-cheese 17, well-roofed 20), 0% near-flat coverage, and only 5% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted brown rather than black. The roof has speckled patches and a darker border, and the counter has a few small items, so it is not a sticker. But the roof is mostly a mid-brown with only about 4 lightness steps, and the counter goods are tiny and sparse. It has fewer tones and less per-item shading than the cheese stall (17) and well (20), with no strong highlight tier, so it looks a little flatter than the best references. Density is slightly lower than the closest same-kind reference, and with doubt resolving to fail, this does not reach the Beodeul bar.

The candidate has 10 visible tones per tile, about level with the simple hedge (9) but well under the closest same-kind reference, prop-stall-cheese (17), and prop-well-roofed (20).
